rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~97% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); RBA Dec hold ~99%; BoC Dec ~80% (Reuters); BoE Dec ~82%; ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%
rows.read: A December Fed hike stays fully priced after strong US growth and slightly hot core inflation, so the dollar needs bets on further hikes to rise much more. Hot Australian inflation ended talk of a cut there, and Canada and the UK still lean toward December hikes.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US Q3 GDP +4.3% annualized, second estimate (fcst 3.5%, advance 3.4%); jobless claims 189K (fcst 201K); spending Oct +0.3% (fcst 0.4%); Germany Q3 GDP +0.1% q/q final
rows.read: The US economy grew at a 4.3% annual pace in July to September, far faster than first reported, while Germany managed just 0.1%. That gap keeps money flowing toward the dollar. Jobless claims stayed low, though spending was a little soft in October.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US core PCE Oct +0.3% m/m, +3.3% y/y (fcst 3.2%); Australia CPI Oct 4.9% y/y (fcst 4.7%), trimmed mean 3.8%; BoJ core CPI 2.3% (fcst 2.5%)
rows.read: US core inflation ticked up to 3.3% a year in October, a touch above forecast, and Australian inflation jumped to 4.9%. Both keep their central banks from easing. Japan's core measure cooled slightly but stays above target.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Reports that the Trump administration is about to unveil new tariffs on 16 trading partners sent Nasdaq futures down more than 2%. The Aussie and kiwi fell hardest. Gold slid too, a sign that higher US rates still outweigh fear.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$90.89 (−0.56%), Tuesday settle $91.40; WTI ~$81.48; gold ~$3,500, a 14-month low
rows.read: Oil held near $91 as Iran's unconfirmed mine claims offset plentiful supply, which leaves the Canadian dollar without a lift. Gold's fall to a 14-month low takes support away from Australia's export earnings.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: USTR Section 301 findings expected soon, 16 partners, final rates not set (Reuters); US 10-year ~4.90% (Hercules, WSJ); S&P France review Fri Nov 27 (Hercules)
rows.read: The US is expected to unveil new tariffs on 16 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan, which could weigh on their economies and on US growth. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs high. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating on Friday.
